recognize_zh: 視野中有兩條細長彎曲的線狀蟲體，紫藍色體部內含密集核柱，兩端外有淡粉紅色、超出蟲體的鞘膜（sheath），大小遠大於背景紅血球；在嗜酸性球增多病人的 buffy coat 抹片中出現有鞘微絲蟲（microfilaria）。此圖為螢幕翻拍並有條紋干擾，尾端核的分布無法清楚判讀。
features: Two long, slender, curved worm-like organisms many times longer than an RBC diameter
Bodies stain dark blue-purple with a densely packed column of nuclei
Pale pink sheath extending beyond the head and tail ends of the bodies
Tail-end nuclear pattern and cephalic space not resolvable due to image quality
Background of RBC-rich buffy coat material with prominent moiré line artifact from photographing a screen
describe_en: Buffy coat smear shows two elongated, curved microfilariae lying across a background of red cells. The organisms have a dark blue-purple body packed with nuclei and a pale pink sheath that projects beyond the anterior and posterior ends. Evaluation of the cephalic space and the arrangement of terminal tail nuclei, which is needed for species identification, is limited by moiré artifact and resolution. Findings are consistent with sheathed microfilariae in buffy coat; species determination requires a thick film or concentrated specimen at higher resolution, ideally with nocturnal sampling, or molecular testing.

ddx.vs: W. bancrofti is sheathed but its sheath often stains poorly with Giemsa, the body curves gently and the tail tip is free of nuclei.
B. malayi has a sheath that stains pink with Giemsa, kinked body curves and two distinct separated terminal tail nuclei, which cannot be confirmed in this image.
Loa loa is sheathed with a sheath that stains poorly with Giemsa and nuclei extending continuously to the tail tip, and circulates by day.
Mansonella microfilariae are smaller and unsheathed with a blunt tail containing nuclei to the tip.
